messages:
maya: quick thread on continuous-batcher follow-up. i've been thinking about a "soft-quota" surface that prevents oscillation when eviction and admission fight. want feedback on shape.

sanjay: what do you mean by soft-quota vs hard quota?

maya: hard quota is current per-tenant reservation we enforce at admission. soft-quota is a decayable headroom token that eviction can consume without immediate hard drops. it acts as a willingness-to-preempt budget.

liam: interesting. so soft-quota buys time for the scheduler to stabilize rather than immediately preempting?

maya: exactly. when a tenant bursts, coordinator can honor requests up to soft_quota. eviction policy can borrow against soft_quota to nudge heavy tenants, but borrowing triggers slow-path signals instead of instant DROPs.

nora: how does this interact with KV-cache affinity? if we let heavy tenant use cache via soft-quota, we might thrash KV locality.
maya: we should include affinity_penalty in the accounting. per-batch we expose: tenant_id, seq_len_est, kv_locality_score, soft_quota_delta. eviction policy sees a combined cost = token_cost * (1 + affinity_penalty).

jen: want to call out states. propose: OPEN, PINNED (reserved kv), QUEUED, DISPATCHING, UPLOADING, RUNNING, CANCELLED. coordinator exposes state transitions so eviction can reason about upload costs.

sanjay: upload-aware preemption is critical. preempting during UPLOADING should have a cost/benefit check. maybe policy gets upload_time_ms and expected remaining_tokens to compute waste.

liam: how are eviction decisions communicated? we had webhook style or shared memory earlier. i'd prefer a synchronized decision queue to keep race surface minimal.

maya: agreed. design: eviction service writes decisions to a lock-free ring buffer with sequences. coordinator applies decisions during a single CAS on batch.state. if CAS fails, decision skipped and we emit a metric.

nora: ring buffer + CAS seems fine. what about prioritized preempt: prefer trimming large batches from noisy tenants vs dropping tiny low-cost batches?
maya: policy can return ACTIONS: NOOP, TRIM(n_tokens), PREEMPT_WITH_GRACE(ms), DROP. trimming implies we mutate batch.token_budget and requeue remainder. coordinator must support partial-trim semantics.

jen: partial trims raise billing/consistency questions. what does user see if we trim a generation mid-stream? must map to partial response or restart. we need UX hooks.

maya: agreed; for trimmed responses we will return a 206-like partial result with a reason header and a retry token. billing will attribute consumed tokens. jen, add billing tag spec?

jen: will do. another ops angle: we need a circuit breaker if eviction churn > threshold. proposal: if > X preempts/sec globally, flip to conservative mode for T seconds (no trims, only NOOP/DROP).

ops-bot: reminder: canary window is Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. keep rollout small.

liam: simulation plan: build a microbench that spawns tenants with Zipf distribution of sizes, inject kvcache-residency correlation, and run scheduler with different soft_quota decay rates. measure tail latency, preempt_rate, churn.
sanjay: add a lattice fairness baseline (virtual time fairness) as a comparator. want to see where soft-quota beats simple virtual-time.

nora: argue for an observability event: batch_snapshot. includes batch_id, state, tenant_id, token_est, kv_score, soft_quota_balance, last_eviction_action. SSE stream for debugging.
maya: good. also emit tenant_window_usage (last_60s_tokens) and tenant_inflight_tokens. these are read-only for eviction policy.

liam: question: how do we version policy contract? if policy returns TRIM with a new field in future, coordinator must ignore unknown fields. use proto with enums and unknown field-safe semantics.
maya: proto + semantic version in ring buffer message. coordinator validates major version match on startup. upgrade path: staggered to feature-flagged nodes.

sanjay: one tricky case: back-to-back preempts causing requeue storms. mitigation: when a batch is trimmed/dropped we tag tenant with a cooling_period_millis; coordinator rejects re-enqueues that would exceed cooling rate.

jen: cooling needs to be per-route too. some routes are high priority customer-facing; others are background. policy should be route-aware.

maya: yep add route_id to accounting. final ask: liam/nora/sanjay can you review proto sketch and the microbench script? i'll open PR with doc and example policy (soft_quota + affinity penalty) tomorrow.

liam: i'll take the microbench.
sanjay: i'll review proto.
nora: will look at observability schema.
maya: thanks all. if no objections i'll land draft next week. :thumbsup:
